hook_text: Could a driver's wrong turn help start a world war?
clip_script: Sarajevo, 28 June 1914. A bomb misses the archduke's car. Hours later, his driver takes the wrong street and stops to reverse, right beside nineteen-year-old Gavrilo Princip. Two shots. Franz Ferdinand and Sophie are dead. Then the dominoes fall: Germany's blank cheque, the ultimatum, war on Serbia on 28 July, Russia mobilises, Germany marches through Belgium. On 4 August Britain declares war. Thirty-seven days. The shot was the spark; the powder had been building for years.
visual_style: A whiteboard street map of Sarajevo with the car's route and wrong turn, then a row of dominoes labelled with countries falling across a map of Europe.
pacing: Builds from the shot to the cascade of declarations.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master the immediate cause of the First World War.
